rules.rule:
This file loads and validates the user-owned `panel.toml`. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep the default config paths (`~/.agent-ops/panel.toml`), output root (`~/.agent-ops/audits`), and state dir (`~/.agent-ops/state`) overridable via `AGENT_OPS_HOME`.
- Keep every numeric default (`DEFAULT_MAX_PAYLOAD=400_000`, `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=8000`, `DEFAULT_LEASE_SLOTS=1`) defined as a documented constant, not an inline literal.

## Documentation Sync
- Any change to the `[agent_ops]` table schema (e.g. adding/removing `max_payload`, `max_tokens`, `lease_slots`, `state_dir`, `outroot`) must update `README.md` § Requirements/Install/Use, `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` if it touches failure modes, and `panel.example.toml`.
- The comment on `DEFAULT_LEASE_SLOTS` documents account contention: `"One panel at a time. Concurrency against a rate-limited endpoint does not fail cleanly — it queues, and the tail grows until a seat blows its budget."` (`config.py:55-56`). Do not silently drop or weaken this comment when changing lease logic; if the default or behavior changes, the comment and `panel.example.toml` must change together.

## Test Coverage
- Any new config key MUST be validated with a type/positive-integer check and a test in `tests/test_config.py`. Any change to default values must update `tests/test_init.py` or the shipped-tree tests if they assert on the example config.

This file implements the review CLI, payload building, panel selection, lease acquisition, seat execution, and summary emission. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep the `--scope` / `--only` / `--split-by-file` scoping behavior: `--only` is ONE path substring, `--split-by-file` runs one panel per changed file sequentially under one lease.
- Keep the exit-code contract (0 = panel convened and at least one seat reported; 1 = nothing reviewed or split run left files unreviewed; 2 = config/git/provider/ref; 3 = refused secret; 7 = lease held; 8 = cancelled; 130 = killed).
- Keep the summary written on every exit path, including the ones that produce no report directory.

## Documentation Sync
- Any change to the exit-code table, the `--only` semantics, or the `--split-by-file` behavior must update `README.md` § "Exit codes" and "Use".
- Any change to the payload truncation behavior (`max_payload`, the `[TRUNCATED at …]` marker, the soft note at `SEAT_NOTE_CHARS`) must update `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` rules 1 and 8 and the README discussion of scoped payloads.

## Test Coverage
- New CLI flags or changed defaults must have coverage in `tests/test_main.py`. Changes to `--split-by-file` must have coverage in the split-file tests. Dead-seat and truncation handling must keep their existing tests.

This file builds the exact text that leaves the machine for a review. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep `DEFAULT_MAX_PAYLOAD = 400_000` as the truncation threshold and `SEAT_NOTE_CHARS = 20_000` as the soft-note threshold.
- Keep `run_git` raising `GitError` on every failure and never returning an empty string for a failed invocation.

## Documentation Sync
- Any change to `DEFAULT_MAX_PAYLOAD`, the truncation marker, or the `--only`/`exact` scoping rules must update `README.md` and `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` rules 1 and 8, because the playbook explicitly warns about payloads over ~150k chars hitting shell argument limits and truncated reports being partial audits.

## Test Coverage
- Payload edge cases (new unreadable files, deleted files, substring-vs-exact `only`, UnicodeDecodeError handling) must keep their tests in `tests/test_payload.py`.

This file selects the panel of seats and excludes the coder's family. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep the rule that a model must never review its own family's work; do not add an opt-out or override that defeats family exclusion.
- Keep dead-seat detection (empty body, timeout, transport error, truncation) distinct from agreement.

## Documentation Sync
- Any change to seat selection, probing, or dead-seat classification must update `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` rules 2, 3, 4, and 9 and the README `probe` / seat descriptions.

## Test Coverage
- Changes to family exclusion or dead-seat logic must update `tests/test_panel.py` and the fake-provider tests in `tests/test_main.py`.

This file implements cooperative lease acquisition so panels stay serial against shared endpoints. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep the lease serial-by-default (`DEFAULT_LEASE_SLOTS=1`). Do not raise the default concurrency cap without explicit measurement and documentation.

## Documentation Sync
- The comment on `DEFAULT_LEASE_SLOTS` in `config.py` and the `lease_slots` value in `panel.example.toml` must stay consistent. If `lease_slots` becomes configurable in a new way, document the account-contention rationale (`config.py:55-56`, `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` rule 9) and never silently drop it.

## Test Coverage
- Lease behavior changes must update `tests/test_lease.py`.

This file formats seat reports and appends run statistics. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep the `# ⚠️ TRUNCATED` header and the `# ⛔ SEAT DID NOT RUN` header worded exactly as the classify/summary code expects.

## Documentation Sync
- Any change to report headers or the stats JSONL schema must update `README.md` CI-gate examples and `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` rule 8 (TRUNCATED means partial).

## Test Coverage
- Report format changes must update `tests/test_summary.py` and any test that parses report files.

This is the user-facing documentation. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep the install paths, the panel setup commands, the exit-code table, and the CI gate example consistent with the code.

## Documentation Sync
- Any documented command, flag, or config key must exist in the code. Do not describe `--only` as taking a list; it takes one path substring.
- The three failure modes from `docs/PLAYBOOK.md` (payloads over ~150k chars hitting argument-list-too-long, TRUNCATED reports being partial, ~1/3 of findings being false positives with line/position drift) must remain referenced when describing scoped payloads and how to read reports.

## Test Coverage
- README command examples should be runnable; if a code change breaks an example, fix the README.

This is the operating manual for reading panel output. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep the rules ordered by damage caused and keep each rule tied to a real recorded failure.

## Documentation Sync
- Any code change that addresses or changes a failure mode documented here (clean exit vs clean audit, dead seats, family exclusion, scoped payload limits, truncation, false-positive rates, lease contention) must update the matching rule and add a regression test.

## Test Coverage
- A playbook change that adds a new failure mode should ideally be paired with a test or at least a code change that makes the failure detectable.

This file is the reference panel configuration. When reviewing changes here, enforce ALL of the following:

## Style Consistency
- Keep `[agent_ops].lease_slots = 1` and its comment about account contention unless the default changes, in which case update `core/agent_ops/config.py` and `README.md` together.

## Documentation Sync
- Any added seat/provider example must be consistent with the provider types supported by `config.py` and the provider implementation in `core/agent_ops/providers.py`.

## Test Coverage
- `tests/test_config.py` and `tests/test_shipped_tree.py` assert this file parses and matches the defaults; update them when the example changes.
